correctness.rationale: Divisor ideals give the complete vertex list and adjacency rules. Conditioning an independent set on its largest selected B-index m leaves exactly a-m-1 compatible A-vertices and min(m,a-m) compatible lower B-vertices, all mutually nonadjacent. Summation gives the polynomial. Maximality forces every compatible vertex, yielding all a+1 facets and their sizes.

value.rationale: The full independence polynomial and maximal-facet classification give a complete enumerative description of independent ideal families in a natural infinite arithmetic class. They simultaneously yield the maximum-independent-set count, well-covered threshold, and independent domination number, with a uniform symbolic proof rather than isolated computation.
